_comment: Human-authored context merged in by scripts/generate-db-docs.js when you generate a database reference on demand (npm run db:docs; output is NOT committed - see docs/database/README.md). Keys: purpose, status (active|legacy|retired|historical), service (which app/service uses it), sourceOfTruth, danger (data-safety note). Tables not listed here are documented from structure + schema.sql comments alone and default to status 'active'. Update this when you add/retire a table.

groups.purpose: Every Telegram group the bot manages — driver groups, dispatch/office groups, etc. Internal integer `id` is the FK target used everywhere; `telegram_group_id` (bigint) is the real Telegram chat id. `group_type='driver'` + a unit number in `group_name` is how the Samsara integration routes safety-event videos to the right driver group.
groups.danger: Core table referenced by ~30 FKs. Never delete rows to 'clean up' — deactivate with active=false instead. Deleting a group cascades to its chat logs, members, driver profile, etc.

drivers.purpose: Driver identity records keyed by Telegram user id.
drivers.danger: Contains driver PII. Do not delete; deletions cascade to responses.

driver_profiles.purpose: Per-driver-group profile (one active profile per driver group).

bot_users.purpose: Everyone the bot sees — button tappers (interactions) and anyone who texts in a group the bot is in (message_count). Keyed by a stable Telegram user id; enriched with last-seen group/chat, language, source, and linked dispatch team. No message text stored.

dispatch_board_settings.purpose: Single-row (id=1) connection to the external Dispatcher Board (a Google Apps Script web app over the dispatchers' own spreadsheet). `enabled` defaults FALSE and there is no env fallback — nothing is read until an administrator saves an address and a token.
dispatch_board_settings.danger: `token_encrypted` is an AES-256-GCM credential and the board authenticates by putting it in a QUERY STRING. Never log a board URL; `last_error` is written through lib/security/redactUrls.stripUrls and may never contain one.

dispatch_board_rows.purpose: Wenze's snapshot of the Dispatcher Board — one row per board row, keyed by `row_key` (normalised truck + normalised person, because the board has no stable row id). Written ONLY by services/dispatchBoard/poller.js. `person_id`/`link_source`/`link_confidence` are written ONLY by the `board.link_person` correction, never by the poller — and only when the truck and the name independently agree.
dispatch_board_rows.service: bot (poller, consistency sweep, admin feed card)
dispatch_board_rows.sourceOfTruth: The external Dispatcher Board, as of `last_seen_at`. Wenze remains the source of truth for who a person permanently is.
dispatch_board_rows.danger: Contains driver names and phone numbers. A row is NEVER deleted and never marked absent on a failed read — `present=false` plus first/last_seen_at is the only history of an assignment the board itself does not keep.

eld_settings.purpose: Single-row (id=1) ELD/telematics provider credentials (Samsara, Drive HoS, Factor, Leader). Secrets stored AES-256-GCM encrypted.

bol_pod_monitor_settings.purpose: Single-row (id=1) config for the SILENT BOL/POD test monitor: enable flag, test Telegram group id (default -5289094495 = Automatic updating (Test)), and send-unrelated / send-unclear / send-files toggles, plus last_report_at / report_count audit stats. When enabled the bot watches active driver groups, classifies + matches documents, and posts a diagnostic report (and optionally files) to the test group ONLY — never replies in the driver group and NEVER uploads to Datatruck. Values are not secrets.
bol_pod_monitor_settings.service: admin (Settings → BOL/POD Monitor), documentIntakeHandlers (silent monitor), bolPodTestMonitorService
bol_pod_monitor_settings.sourceOfTruth: This table (DB is authoritative — no Render env vars for these values).

gmaps_settings.purpose: Single-row (id=1) Google Maps Platform config for Route Control. Server key encrypted at rest.

message_group_settings.purpose: Single-row (id=1) map of message category → destination Telegram group id (stored as text). Telegram group ids are not secrets. The driver-raise workflow uses TWO independent categories: dispatch_review_group_id for the review REQUEST, raise_results_group_id for the submitted RESULT sent to accounting. No category falls back to another.

ringcentral_settings.purpose: Single-row (id=1) RingCentral call-KPI credentials + thresholds. Secrets encrypted.

safety_event_music_assets.purpose: Uploaded background-music clips for the driver-group speeding-video overlay. Bytes are stored in Postgres BYTEA (storage_kind='db_bytea') because the samsara-integration poller runs as a SEPARATE process with a DIFFERENT Telegram bot and Telegram file_ids are bot-scoped. Exactly one row is active at a time (partial unique index).
safety_event_music_assets.service: admin (Settings → Samsara, writes), samsara-integration (reads active clip bytes)
safety_event_music_assets.danger: Do not hard-delete the active clip — the app refuses it. Deactivate first. The BYTEA is the only copy of the uploaded music.

safety_event_video_settings.purpose: Single-row (id=1) config for the driver-group music overlay: enable flags, active music asset, volume, fades, mix-vs-replace, loop behaviour, and a max-video-length cap. `samsara_notification_group_original_video_enabled` documents (and never overrides) the invariant that the notifications group always gets the original video.

safety_event_video_jobs.purpose: Best-effort observability ledger: one row per driver-group music-overlay attempt (pending→processing→sent/failed/fallback_sent/skipped). Written by the samsara-integration poller.
safety_event_video_jobs.danger: Never store signed media URLs here — only an opaque/masked reference (video_reference).

samsara_processed_events.purpose: Durable dedup set of Samsara safety/speeding event ids already handled, so restarts/redeploys never re-broadcast.

samsara_poll_state.purpose: Key/value poll watermarks + pagination cursors for the two Samsara pollers.

samsara_event_deliveries.purpose: Per-(event, target_chat_id) idempotent delivery ledger — the source of truth for 'already sent, do not resend'. status ∈ delivered|permanent; a delivered row is never downgraded.

driver_location_checkins.danger: Related to the retired check-in/check-out feature (see docs/architecture/retired-checkin-checkout-feature.md). No code reads it. It is no longer created by database/baseline/, so it exists only on deployments that predate 2026-09; its rows are kept until an operator drops it through Settings -> Retired Leftovers, which needs a backup first.

driver_location_monitors.danger: Related to the retired check-in/check-out feature (see docs/architecture/retired-checkin-checkout-feature.md). No code reads it. It is no longer created by database/baseline/, so it exists only on deployments that predate 2026-09; its rows are kept until an operator drops it through Settings -> Retired Leftovers, which needs a backup first.

chat_logs.purpose: Captured Telegram group messages used for AI insights/annotations.
chat_logs.danger: Contains message content (potential PII). Large table — index-sensitive.

leads.purpose: Recruiting leads ingested from external sources (Facebook, Indeed, Bitrix), plus who Bitrix assigned each one to (bitrix_assigned_by_id) and which number actually texted the driver (sms_from_number, sms_sender_recruiter_id).

telegram_document_batches.purpose: Smart BOL/POD intake: one row per batch of related PDF/image attachments a driver sends in their Telegram group. Tracks pipeline lifecycle, AI-detected doc type + confidence, matched Datatruck order/load + match confidence, the inline-confirmation message, and who decided. Restart-safe and idempotent.
telegram_document_batches.danger: No destructive migrations. A batch's files cascade-delete with it.

telegram_document_files.purpose: Smart BOL/POD intake: one row per attached file in a batch. UNIQUE telegram_file_unique_id is the dedup guard; sha256 is the content hash for duplicate-upload prevention and loop detection; sort_order preserves Telegram message order for merged PDFs.

datatruck_upload_attempts.purpose: Smart BOL/POD intake: one row per attempt to upload a confirmed BOL/POD to Datatruck. Records dry-run vs live, returned Datatruck document id, and content hash — used for duplicate-upload prevention and so the Datatruck->Telegram forwarding poller can recognise a bot-originated upload and suppress re-forwarding (loop prevention).

database_transfer_usage.purpose: One row per UTC month recording this application's ESTIMATE of the bytes it has read from the database, so the admin panel can warn at 80/90/95% of the hosted monthly transfer allowance instead of discovering the ceiling when reads start failing. Written by database/transferUsage.js from the in-memory counters in database/transferMeter.js (sampled result sizes, extrapolated); read once at boot so a Render restart does not reset the month.
database_transfer_usage.sourceOfTruth: This table, for the app's own estimate only. The provider's dashboard is the authority on billed transfer; these numbers are never an invoice.
database_transfer_usage.danger: Keep its own write volume negligible — one UPSERT a minute. A meter that wrote per query would consume the budget it measures. Truncating it only loses the current month’s estimate; nothing else depends on it.

ringcentral_connect_sessions.purpose: Short-lived, single-use links a recruiter opens to authorize RingCentral for their OWN number (/ringcentral/connect/:token). The token in the URL is the credential — these routes carry no admin session — so it expires in 30 minutes, is consumed on success, and oauth_state binds the redirect we sent to the callback we accept. Modeled on facebook_connect_sessions.
ringcentral_connect_sessions.danger: session_token and oauth_state are bearer credentials — never log them, never render them into a page other than the link handed to the invited recruiter.

recruiters.purpose: One row per recruiter: their dedicated RingCentral direct number, the credentials that let the app act AS them (an OAuth refresh token from /ringcentral/connect, preferred, or a pasted JWT), and bitrix_user_id — the link that makes a Facebook lead assigned to them in Bitrix24 get texted from their number.
recruiters.service: bot-backend (lead auto-SMS, recruiterCallSyncService, ringCentralTokenRefreshService), admin Settings → RingCentral
recruiters.danger: refresh_token_encrypted ROTATES: a RingCentral refresh grant invalidates the token it was called with, so this column is rewritten on every refresh. Restoring an old backup of this row re-installs a dead token and the recruiter silently stops sending. jwt/client secrets are AES-256-GCM (lib/security/facebookCrypto.js) — never returned raw by the API.

facebook_lead_sms_mirrors.purpose: Links a Telegram message to the driver phone it mirrors, so a reply typed in the group is relayed as an SMS exactly once. recruiter_id/from_number record WHICH of our numbers the conversation is on, so the reply leaves from the same number that first texted the driver.

bitrix_settings.purpose: Single-row (id=1) Bitrix24 CRM settings edited in Settings → RingCentral → Bitrix24: enabled, inbound webhook (encrypted — the URL path IS the credential, never returned to a browser), entity, assignee at creation, source, deal pipeline, assignee wait. Every column NULL = inherit the BITRIX24_* env var; the DB row wins once set. assigned_by_id is TEXT so '' (explicitly nobody) differs from NULL (inherit).

facebook_lead_recruiter_messages.purpose: Optional per-recruiter override of the Facebook-lead auto-SMS text, keyed by recruiter_id. Blank or absent means 'use the global time-based Auto Message system' — that is why the admin API deletes a row rather than storing an empty string.
facebook_lead_recruiter_messages.service: admin (edited), bot (read when a lead's Bitrix assignee is resolved)
facebook_lead_recruiter_messages.danger: ON DELETE CASCADE from recruiters. Removing a row is safe — the lead falls back to the global message.

samsara_settings.purpose: One row (id=1) holding the Samsara connection (API key, base URL, enabled), the safety-event switches and every missing-video recovery control. THE CONFIGURATION CHANNEL between bot-backend and the separate samsara-integration poller, which reads it over the shared database.
samsara_settings.sourceOfTruth: This table; every column falls back to the matching environment variable when empty, so an existing deployment keeps working untouched.
samsara_settings.danger: api_key_encrypted uses lib/security/sharedIntegrationCrypto (NOT facebookCrypto) because the poller must open it too. Never return it to a browser. Clearing it hands Samsara back to SAMSARA_API_KEY — if none is set, Samsara stops.

samsara_video_recovery_jobs.purpose: The durable queue of safety events alerted WITHOUT dashcam video: the Telegram messages to fold the clip into, the Samsara retrieval being waited on, the attempt count and a terminal state. Replaced an in-memory timer that lost every pending video on a redeploy.
samsara_video_recovery_jobs.service: samsara-integration (writes and works them), admin (read-only diagnostics)
samsara_video_recovery_jobs.sourceOfTruth: samsara-integration; bot-backend owns the DDL (migration 0013) and only reads.
samsara_video_recovery_jobs.danger: samsara_event_id is UNIQUE and enqueue is ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING — that is what stops a re-delivered event creating a second recovery and a duplicate Samsara retrieval request. Never store a signed media URL in targets or last_error.

control_settings.purpose: Single row (id=1) for the control channel: whether Wenze may ask questions in Telegram at all, how many one sweep may ask (`max_questions_per_pass`), how long before an unanswered question may be repeated (`repeat_after_hours`), and how many times it may come back with 'why?' (`clarify_limit`).
control_settings.service: bot (ask pass, reply handler, admin settings card)
control_settings.sourceOfTruth: This row. A missing table reads as the defaults rather than as an error, so a deploy where the migration has not yet run behaves identically.
control_settings.danger: `enabled = FALSE` makes every reply in the group silent — recorded, never acted on and never answered. That is the intended off switch, but it looks exactly like a broken channel from inside Telegram.

control_operators.purpose: WHO WENZE OBEYS in a notification group. Numeric Telegram user ids only. Seeded by migration 0048 with `CREATOR_USER_ID` from bot/creatorMessageManager.js and nobody else.
control_operators.sourceOfTruth: This table, absolutely. Telegram group membership and Telegram's own admin flags grant nothing.
control_operators.danger: This is the only thing between a reply in a group chat and a correction to the fleet. A row added here can approve identity and home-time corrections. A degraded read answers NO — the one place in the repository where a failed read must refuse rather than fall back to a default. The last enabled row cannot be removed: an empty table means nobody can steer Wenze from Telegram.

control_replies.purpose: Every reply to an operational question — obeyed, refused or ignored — with what it was read as and what it did. `UNIQUE (chat_id, reply_message_id)` is the redelivery guard, claimed BEFORE anything is acted on.
control_replies.service: bot (reply handler), admin (finding detail, health counts)
control_replies.sourceOfTruth: The record of what was said in Telegram and what Wenze did about it. The correction itself lives in operational_corrections and the reasoning in operational_decisions.
control_replies.danger: Contains text a person typed into a group chat, capped at 1000 characters. Only counts leave through /api/health, never text. Without the UNIQUE constraint a redelivered 'yes' applies the same correction twice.

driver_person_telegram_identities.purpose: Which Telegram account belongs to which PERSON, over time. `driver_profiles.telegram_user_id` answers the same question about a CHAT and is lost when the chat is recreated; this survives it. Backfilled from that column at confidence 100, because a value typed in by an administrator is the strongest evidence in the system.
driver_person_telegram_identities.service: bot (the consistency sweep's telegram-identity check and its correction), admin (person panel)
driver_person_telegram_identities.sourceOfTruth: This table, for who is behind an account. `uniq_person_telegram_open_account` is the anchor: ONE OPEN ROW PER ACCOUNT — one human per account at a time. The constraint is on the account and not the person, because somebody may carry a second phone.
driver_person_telegram_identities.danger: Contains Telegram account ids. Counts only leave through /api/health, and no id ever appears in a finding title or a notice — those reach a group chat's permanent history. A row is CLOSED, never deleted: an account that moved owners leaves a trail, and that trail is the point. `username_at_link` is a snapshot and is never matched on, because a username is reassignable.
